title.en: Advanced Verb Patterns (regret to / regret -ing, go on, be used to)
title.es: Patrones verbales avanzados (regret to / regret -ing, go on, be used to)

text.en: After many verbs comes an -ing form or a to-infinitive, and the two patterns can differ in meaning. Regret to inform means: I am sorry that I am telling you now. Regret telling means: I am sorry that I told someone earlier. Go on and mean work the same way; be used to is different: its to is a preposition, so -ing always follows. After other verbs only the -ing form follows (can’t help, it’s no use), and for others an object changes the pattern: “We don’t allow smoking.” but “We don’t allow people to smoke.” Spanish often uses a plain infinitive for this, so the English patterns must be learned word by word.
text.es: Después de muchos verbos va una forma -ing o un to-infinitivo, y los dos patrones pueden cambiar el significado. Regret to inform significa: lamento comunicarle ahora. Regret telling significa: me arrepiento de haberlo dicho antes. Go on y mean funcionan igual; be used to es distinto: su to es una preposición, por eso siempre va -ing. Después de otros verbos solo va -ing (can’t help, it’s no use), y en otros un objeto cambia el patrón: «We don’t allow smoking.» pero «We don’t allow people to smoke.» El español suele usar un simple infinitivo para esto, por eso hay que aprender los patrones del inglés palabra por palabra.

rows: luego pasar a otra cosa (go on + ...)

title.en: Regret, go on, mean: two patterns, two meanings
title.es: Regret, go on, mean: dos patrones, dos significados

text.en: Regret + to-infinitive: sorry to say now (formal news). Regret + -ing: sorry that you did it. Go on + -ing: continue. Go on + to-infinitive: then do something new. Mean + -ing: involve. Mean + to-infinitive: intend.
text.es: Regret + to-infinitivo: lamento decir ahora (noticia formal). Regret + -ing: me arrepiento de haberlo hecho. Go on + -ing: continuar. Go on + to-infinitivo: luego hacer algo nuevo. Mean + -ing: implicar. Mean + to-infinitivo: tener la intención.

examples.es: I regret to inform you that you were not accepted.

tr.en: I regret to inform you that you were not accepted.
tr.es: Lamento informarle que no fue aceptado.

examples.es: I regret telling him my secret.

tr.en: I regret telling him my secret.
tr.es: Me arrepiento de haberle contado mi secreto.

text.en: Go on talking: he continues the same thing. Go on to become: as a next step he becomes something. “This will mean moving” means it involves moving.
text.es: Go on talking: sigue con lo mismo. Go on to become: como siguiente paso llega a ser algo. «This will mean moving» significa que implica mudarse.

examples.es: He went on talking for two hours.

tr.en: He went on talking for two hours.
tr.es: Siguió hablando dos horas.

examples.es: Taking the job will mean moving to another city.

tr.en: Taking the job will mean moving to another city.
tr.es: Aceptar el trabajo implicará mudarse a otra ciudad.

title.en: Be used to / get used to + -ing and used to + base verb
title.es: Be used to / get used to + -ing y used to + verbo base

text.en: After be used to and get used to the to is a preposition, so an -ing form follows: “I’m used to getting up early.” Used to + base verb is a past habit: “I used to smoke.”
text.es: Después de be used to y get used to el to es una preposición, por eso sigue una forma -ing: «I’m used to getting up early.» Used to + verbo base es un hábito pasado: «I used to smoke.»

examples.es: I'm not used to getting up early.

tr.en: I'm not used to getting up early.
tr.es: No estoy acostumbrado a levantarme temprano.

examples.es: She used to live in London.

tr.en: She used to live in London.
tr.es: Ella vivía en Londres.

text.en: These are always followed by -ing: can’t help, it’s no use, it’s worth, there’s no point in, have difficulty (in), be busy, spend time. Need + -ing has a passive meaning: “The windows need cleaning.”
text.es: Siempre les sigue -ing: can’t help, it’s no use, it’s worth, there’s no point in, have difficulty (in), be busy, spend time. Need + -ing tiene sentido pasivo: «The windows need cleaning.»

tr.en: I can't help laughing.
tr.es: No puedo evitar reírme.

examples.es: It's no use worrying about the past.

tr.en: It's no use worrying about the past.
tr.es: No sirve de nada preocuparse por el pasado.

title.en: Object + -ing, object + base verb and the allow type
title.es: Objeto + -ing, objeto + verbo base y el tipo allow

text.en: A perception verb + object + -ing: in progress; the base verb: the whole action. Catch / find + object + -ing: to find someone doing something. Allow and permit take -ing without an object, a to-infinitive with an object.
text.es: Un verbo de percepción + objeto + -ing: en proceso; el verbo base: la acción completa. Catch / find + objeto + -ing: sorprender a alguien haciendo algo. Allow y permit llevan -ing sin objeto, un to-infinitivo con objeto.

examples.es: We saw the thieves running out of the house.

tr.en: We saw the thieves running out of the house.
tr.es: Vimos a los ladrones salir corriendo de la casa.

examples.es: They don't allow people to smoke in the library.

tr.en: They don't allow people to smoke in the library.
tr.es: En la biblioteca no permiten que la gente fume.

text.en: Without an object: “They don’t allow smoking in the library.” Caught him stealing means: I found him in the act of stealing.
text.es: Sin objeto: «They don’t allow smoking in the library.» Caught him stealing significa: lo sorprendí robando.

examples.es: They don't allow smoking in the library.

tr.en: They don't allow smoking in the library.
tr.es: En la biblioteca no permiten fumar.

examples.es: I caught him stealing the cookies.

tr.en: I caught him stealing the cookies.
tr.es: Lo sorprendí robándose las galletas.

text.en: Spanish influence: not “I’m used to drive”, but “I’m used to driving”. The Spanish “solía vivir” is used to live: after used to (habit) there is always the base verb.
text.es: Influencia del español: no «I’m used to drive», sino «I’m used to driving». El «solía vivir» del español es used to live: después de used to (hábito) siempre va el verbo base.

text.en: Allow does not take “to + verb” without an object: not “They don’t allow to smoke”, but “They don’t allow smoking” or “They don’t allow people to smoke”.
text.es: Allow no admite «to + verbo» sin objeto: no «They don’t allow to smoke», sino «They don’t allow smoking» o «They don’t allow people to smoke».

speak.en: After many verbs comes an -ing form or a to-infinitive, and the meaning can differ. «Regret to inform» means I am sorry to tell you now. «Regret telling» means I am sorry I told someone. «Go on talking» means to continue, «go on to become» means a next step. After «be used to» comes -ing: «I'm used to getting up early». After «used to» comes the base verb: «I used to smoke». «Allow» takes -ing without an object: «They don't allow smoking».
speak.es: Después de muchos verbos va una forma -ing o un to-infinitivo, y el significado puede cambiar. «Regret to inform» significa lamento decirlo ahora. «Regret telling» significa me arrepiento de haberlo dicho. «Go on talking» significa continuar, «go on to become» significa un siguiente paso. Después de «be used to» va -ing: «I'm used to getting up early». Después de «used to» va el verbo base: «I used to smoke». «Allow» sin objeto lleva -ing: «They don't allow smoking».

items.sentence: I regret ___ you that your application was unsuccessful.

why.en: Giving formal news now: regret to inform.
why.es: Dar una noticia formal ahora: regret to inform.

inform.en: “Regret inform” is not correct; after regret comes to + base verb or -ing.
inform.es: «Regret inform» no es correcto; después de regret va to + verbo base o -ing.

to informing.en: “Regret to informing” is not correct; after to you need the base verb.
to informing.es: «Regret to informing» no es correcto; después de to hace falta el verbo base.

examples: I regret to tell you this.

tr.en: I regret to inform you that your application was unsuccessful.
tr.es: Lamento informarle que su solicitud no tuvo éxito.

items.sentence: I regret ___ him my secret; now everyone knows.

why.en: Sorry about what you did earlier: regret + -ing.
why.es: Arrepentirse de lo que hiciste antes: regret + -ing.

tell.en: “Regret tell” is not correct; after regret comes to + base verb or -ing.
tell.es: «Regret tell» no es correcto; después de regret va to + verbo base o -ing.

told.en: “Regret told” is not correct; after regret you need the -ing form.
told.es: «Regret told» no es correcto; después de regret hace falta la forma -ing.

tr.en: I regret telling him my secret; now everyone knows.
tr.es: Me arrepiento de haberle contado mi secreto; ahora todo el mundo lo sabe.

items.sentence: He went on ___ for two hours without a break.

talk.en: “Went on talk” is not correct; after go on comes -ing or to + base verb.
talk.es: «Went on talk» no es correcto; después de go on va -ing o to + verbo base.

talked.en: “Went on talked” is not correct; after go on comes -ing or to + base verb.
talked.es: «Went on talked» no es correcto; después de go on va -ing o to + verbo base.

tr.en: He went on talking for two hours without a break.
tr.es: Él siguió hablando por dos horas sin parar.

items.sentence: After serving as mayor, she went on ___ the new minister.

why.en: The next step: go on + to-infinitive.
why.es: El siguiente paso: go on + to-infinitivo.

become.en: “Went on become” is not correct; the to cannot be dropped.
become.es: «Went on become» no es correcto; el to no se puede omitir.

became.en: “Went on became” is not correct; after go on comes to + base verb or -ing.
became.es: «Went on became» no es correcto; después de go on va to + verbo base o -ing.

tr.en: After serving as mayor, she went on to become the new minister.
tr.es: Después de ser alcaldesa, pasó a ser la nueva ministra.

items.sentence: Taking the job will mean ___ to another city.

move.en: “Will mean move” is not correct; in this meaning you need -ing.
move.es: «Will mean move» no es correcto; en este sentido hace falta -ing.

moved.en: “Will mean moved” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
moved.es: «Will mean moved» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

tr.en: Taking the job will mean moving to another city.
tr.es: Aceptar el trabajo significará mudarse a otra ciudad.

hurt.en: “Didn’t mean hurt” is not correct; the to cannot be dropped.
hurt.es: «Didn’t mean hurt» no es correcto; el to no se puede omitir.

hurts.en: “Didn’t mean hurts” is not correct; after didn’t comes the base verb.
hurts.es: «Didn’t mean hurts» no es correcto; después de didn’t va el verbo base.

examples: I didn't mean to be rude.

tr.en: I didn't mean to hurt you.
tr.es: No quise lastimarte.

items.sentence: They spent the whole evening ___ about money.

why.en: After spend time comes the -ing form.
why.es: Después de spend time va la forma -ing.

to argue.en: “Spent the evening to argue” is not correct; after spending time you need -ing.
to argue.es: «Spent the evening to argue» no es correcto; después de pasar tiempo hace falta -ing.

argue.en: “Spent the evening argue” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
argue.es: «Spent the evening argue» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

tr.en: They spent the whole evening arguing about money.
tr.es: Se pasaron toda la noche discutiendo por dinero.

items.sentence: I have difficulty ___ in noisy rooms.

why.en: After have difficulty comes the -ing form.
why.es: Después de have difficulty va la forma -ing.

to concentrate.en: “Have difficulty to concentrate” is not correct (Spanish influence); you need -ing.
to concentrate.es: «Have difficulty to concentrate» no es correcto (influencia del español); hace falta -ing.

concentrate.en: “Have difficulty concentrate” is not correct; you need the -ing form.
concentrate.es: «Have difficulty concentrate» no es correcto; hace falta la forma -ing.

tr.en: I have difficulty concentrating in noisy rooms.
tr.es: Tengo dificultad para concentrarme en habitaciones ruidosas.

items.sentence: I can't help ___ when I see that video.

why.en: After can’t help comes the -ing form.
why.es: Después de can’t help va la forma -ing.

to laugh.en: “Can’t help to laugh” is not correct; you need -ing.
to laugh.es: «Can’t help to laugh» no es correcto; hace falta -ing.

laugh.en: “Can’t help laugh” is not correct; you need -ing.
laugh.es: «Can’t help laugh» no es correcto; hace falta -ing.

tr.en: I can't help laughing when I see that video.
tr.es: No puedo evitar reírme cuando veo ese video.

items.sentence: It's no use ___ about the past.

why.en: After it’s no use comes the -ing form.
why.es: Después de it’s no use va la forma -ing.

to worry.en: “It’s no use to worry” is not the standard pattern; you need -ing.
to worry.es: «It’s no use to worry» no es el patrón estándar; hace falta -ing.

worry.en: “It’s no use worry” is not correct; you need -ing.
worry.es: «It’s no use worry» no es correcto; hace falta -ing.

tr.en: It's no use worrying about the past.
tr.es: No sirve de nada preocuparse por el pasado.

items.sentence: There's no point in ___ if he won't listen.

why.en: After there’s no point in comes the -ing form.
why.es: Después de there’s no point in va la forma -ing.

to talk.en: After in there is no to-infinitive; you need -ing.
to talk.es: Después de in no va to-infinitivo; hace falta -ing.

talk.en: After in the base verb does not stand; you need -ing.
talk.es: Después de in el verbo base no va; hace falta -ing.

tr.en: There's no point in talking if he won't listen.
tr.es: No tiene caso hablar si él no va a escuchar.

why.es: Después de worth va la forma -ing.

to keep.en: “Worth to keep” is not correct; after worth you need -ing.
to keep.es: «Worth to keep» no es correcto; después de worth hace falta -ing.

keep.en: “Worth keep” is not correct; after worth you need -ing.
keep.es: «Worth keep» no es correcto; después de worth hace falta -ing.

tr.en: The old car is worth keeping.
tr.es: Vale la pena conservar el carro viejo.

items.sentence: We saw the thieves ___ out of the house.

why.en: A perception verb + object + -ing: in progress.
why.es: Un verbo de percepción + objeto + -ing: en proceso.

to run.en: After a perception verb there is no to-infinitive.
to run.es: Después de un verbo de percepción no va to-infinitivo.

ran.en: “Saw them ran” is not correct; you need -ing or the base verb.
ran.es: «Saw them ran» no es correcto; hace falta -ing o el verbo base.

tr.en: We saw the thieves running out of the house.
tr.es: Vimos a los ladrones salir corriendo de la casa.

why.en: After catch + object comes the -ing form.
why.es: Después de catch + objeto va la forma -ing.

to steal.en: “Caught him to steal” is not correct; you need -ing.
to steal.es: «Caught him to steal» no es correcto; hace falta -ing.

steal.en: “Caught him steal” is not correct; you need -ing.
steal.es: «Caught him steal» no es correcto; hace falta -ing.

tr.en: I caught him stealing the cookies.
tr.es: Lo pesqué robándose las galletas.

items.sentence: They don't allow ___ in the library.

why.en: Allow without an object takes the -ing form.
why.es: Allow sin objeto lleva la forma -ing.

to smoke.en: “Allow to smoke” without an object is not correct; you need -ing or object + to.
to smoke.es: «Allow to smoke» sin objeto no es correcto; hace falta -ing u objeto + to.

smoke.en: “Allow smoke” is not correct; you need -ing.
smoke.es: «Allow smoke» no es correcto; hace falta -ing.

tr.en: They don't allow smoking in the library.
tr.es: No permiten fumar en la biblioteca.

items.sentence: They don't allow people ___ in the library.

why.en: After allow + object comes the to-infinitive.
why.es: Después de allow + objeto va el to-infinitivo.

smoking.en: “Allow people smoking” is not the standard pattern; you need to + base verb.
smoking.es: «Allow people smoking» no es el patrón estándar; hace falta to + verbo base.

smoke.en: “Allow people smoke” is not correct; the to is required.
smoke.es: «Allow people smoke» no es correcto; el to es obligatorio.

examples: We do not permit them to park.

tr.en: They don't allow people to smoke in the library.
tr.es: No permiten que la gente fume en la biblioteca.

why.en: Need + -ing has a passive meaning: the windows need cleaning.
why.es: Need + -ing tiene sentido pasivo: the windows need cleaning.

to clean.en: “Windows need to clean” would mean the windows clean something; you need -ing or to be cleaned.
to clean.es: «Windows need to clean» significaría que las ventanas limpian algo; hace falta -ing o to be cleaned.

clean.en: “Windows need clean” is not correct; you need -ing.
clean.es: «Windows need clean» no es correcto; hace falta -ing.

tr.en: The windows need cleaning.
tr.es: Las ventanas necesitan limpieza.

items.es: I regret to tell you the news.

tr.en: I regret to tell you the news.
tr.es: Lamento decirle la noticia.

text.en: sorry about something that already happened
text.es: lamento algo que ya ocurrió

wrong.en: That is the meaning of regret + -ing; regret to goes with news given now.
wrong.es: Ese es el significado de regret + -ing; regret to va con una noticia dada ahora.

text.en: sorry to give the news now
text.es: lamento dar la noticia ahora

text.en: a plan for the future
text.es: un plan para el futuro

wrong.en: Regret to is not a plan but a polite introduction to bad news.
wrong.es: Regret to no es un plan sino una introducción cortés a una mala noticia.

tr.en: I regret telling him.
tr.es: Me arrepiento de habérselo dicho.

text.en: sorry about something I did earlier
text.es: me arrepiento de algo que hice antes

text.en: sorry to say it now
text.es: lamento decirlo ahora

wrong.en: That is the meaning of regret to; regret telling is about a past act.
wrong.es: Ese es el significado de regret to; regret telling trata de un acto pasado.

text.en: an intention
text.es: una intención

wrong.en: Regret telling is not an intention but a regret.
wrong.es: Regret telling no es una intención sino un arrepentimiento.

tr.en: He went on talking.
tr.es: Siguió hablando.

text.en: he started something new
text.es: empezó algo nuevo

wrong.en: For a new action the pattern is go on to + base verb.
wrong.es: Para una acción nueva el patrón es go on to + verbo base.

text.en: he continued the same action
text.es: continuó la misma acción

text.en: he stopped
text.es: dejó de hacerlo

wrong.en: Went on talking is not stopping but continuing.
wrong.es: Went on talking no es dejar de hacer algo sino continuar.

items.es: I'm used to getting up early.

tr.es: Estoy acostumbrado a levantarme temprano.

text.en: used to + base verb: a past habit
text.es: used to + verbo base: un hábito pasado

wrong.en: Here it is be used to + -ing, not a past habit.
wrong.es: Aquí es be used to + -ing, no un hábito pasado.

text.es: be used to + -ing: acostumbrado a algo

text.es: un plan futuro

text.es: lo vi mientras estaba en proceso

text.es: una pregunta
